# Aspen of Part B (`aspen-of-part-b`)

Checks Medicare Part B therapy for nursing-home residents before billing: timed units over the 8-minute rule, missing GP/GO/GN discipline modifiers, lines over the yearly KX threshold without KX, therapy billed to Part B on days the resident was in a Part A stay, and duplicate lines. Resident identifiers are masked before results reach the model.

**Aspen never submits claims.**

Evergreen ver 1 · Billing and revenue cycle · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · resident and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`evergreen-core`](../evergreen-core)

```bash
npx -y aspen-of-part-b demo
npx -y aspen-of-part-b mcp --root ./facility-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional Part B therapy lines, March 2026. KX thresholds of 2,400 are example numbers, not the CMS figures. Planted: R801 4 units for 46 timed minutes (the rule allows 3), R802 2 units for 22 minutes (allows 1), R803 a line with no GP/GO/GN, R804 the yearly PT total passing the threshold without KX (large allowed amounts on purpose), R805 a duplicate line, R806 Part B therapy on a Part A day.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `aspen_check` | List Part B therapy lines that would be denied or overpaid. | runs |
| `aspen_write_report` | Write aspen-part-b.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and aspen-part-b.html into out_dir (default evergreen-out/aspen). | runs |
| `aspen_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `aspen_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `aspen_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `aspen_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `claim_submit` | Aspen never submits claims. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `aspen_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `therapy` (required) | Part B therapy lines under --root: resident, date, CPT, modifiers, timed minutes, units, charge, allowed amount |
| `census` | Optional census under --root, to find lines billed during a Medicare Part A stay |
| `rules` | Optional rules JSON: timed codes and the KX thresholds for the year |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold resident or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx aspen-of-part-b inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Part B therapy lines (`therapy`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `resident_id` | text (masked) | Resident ID, Resident #, Resident Number, Res ID, Res #, MRN, Medical Record Number, Client ID |
| `resident_name` | text (masked) | Resident, Resident Name, Name, Patient, Patient Name, Client Name, Resident Full Name |
| `date` (required) | date | Date, Date of Service, DOS, Service Date |
| `cpt` (required) | text | CPT, Code, Procedure, HCPCS, Procedure Code |
| `modifiers` | text | Modifiers, Modifier, Mods, Modifier 1 |
| `minutes` | number | Minutes, Treatment Minutes, Timed Minutes, Mins |
| `units` | number | Units, Billed Units, Qty |
| `charge` | amount | Charge, Charges, Billed, Amount |
| `allowed` | amount | Allowed, Allowed Amount, Fee Schedule, Expected |

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `resident_id` | text (masked) | Resident ID, Resident #, Resident Number, Res ID, Res #, MRN, Medical Record Number, Client ID |

| `payer` (required) | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Pay Source, Payer Source, Payor, Payor Name, Insurance |
| `payer_type` | text | Payer Type, Payor Type, Payer Class, Payer Category, Pay Type |
| `level` | text | Level, Level of Care, Care Level, Rate Type, Rate Level, Room Type, Accommodation, RUG |

## Settings file (`aspen_rules`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `timed_codes` | Your list of timed (15-minute) codes |
| `kx_threshold_pt_slp` | KX threshold for PT and speech together for the year (set it from the current CMS figure) |
| `kx_threshold_ot` | KX threshold for OT for the year (set it from the current CMS figure) |

## Memory

`aspen_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `aspen_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|
| `timed_code` | adds the code to the 8-minute rule check. It only adds checks. |

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `evergreen-core` and `remedy-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "aspen-of-part-b": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "aspen-of-part-b",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/facility-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add aspen-of-part-b -- npx -y aspen-of-part-b mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
aspen-of-part-b tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
aspen-of-part-b sources               # the columns each input is read from
aspen-of-part-b inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
aspen-of-part-b call aspen_check '{"therapy":"<therapy>"}'
aspen-of-part-b eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
aspen-of-part-b demo
```

## Resident and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: resident and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to PointClickCare, MatrixCare, a payer portal, a bank, a state Medicaid portal or a payroll system.
- Medicare, Medicaid and payroll rules are summarised from public material as of 2026 and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, payroll or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, tax, accounting, clinical, reimbursement or HIPAA advice. A person decides what to bill, pay, appeal, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
